title: Live and fixed imaging of translation sites at single mRNA resolution in the Drosophila embryo
author: Vinter, Hoppe, et al.

steps.title: Load image into Imaris
steps.instruction: Open the whole‑embryo image in Imaris 9.2 (or later). If using a newer version, first run the Imaris File Converter to save the file as *.ims.

steps.title: Create SunTag mRNA spots
steps.instruction: Use the Imaris ‘Spots’ wizard to detect SunTag smFISH mRNA foci with the following settings:

substeps.instruction: Leave the first screen at default.
Select the SunTag smFISH channel.
Estimate XY diameter in Slice view (≈0.6 µm, adjust as needed).
Enable ‘Model PSF‑elongation along Z‑axis’ and ‘Background Subtraction’.
Set Filter Type to ‘Intensity Sum Ch=X Img=1’ (X = SunTag channel) and keep only low‑intensity spots to exclude bright nascent transcription sites.
Add a second filter of type ‘Quality’ and drag until all mRNA spots are selected.
Finish the wizard and name the spots ‘SunTag mRNA spots’.
Verify spot selection on a low‑density region (e.g., edge of expression domain) and toggle the Spots view to ensure no false positives.

steps.title: Create scFv‑mNG spots
steps.instruction: Detect potential translation sites using the Imaris ‘Spots’ wizard with these parameters:

substeps.instruction: Leave the first screen at default.
Select the scFv‑mNG channel.
Estimate XY diameter in Slice view (≈0.5 µm; use the smaller spot size to capture all sites).
Enable ‘Model PSF‑elongation along Z‑axis’ and ‘Background Subtraction’.
Set Filter Type to ‘Quality’ and adjust until all scFv‑mNG foci are captured.
Complete the wizard and name the spots ‘scFv spots’.
If background is high, capture all visually identifiable spots; later colocalization will discard background lacking an mRNA overlap.

steps.title: Colocalize mRNA and scFv spots
steps.instruction: Run the Imaris X‑tension ‘Co‑localize spots’ with a distance threshold of 0.3 µm (300 nm) to define translation sites.

substeps.instruction: Open the ‘X‑tensions’ tab and select ‘Co‑localize spots’.
Choose the two spot masks: ‘SunTag mRNA spots’ and ‘scFv spots’.
Enter threshold = 0.3 (300 nm) and execute.

steps.title: Create nuclear surfaces
steps.instruction: Generate nuclei surfaces (optional for nuclear exclusion) using the Imaris ‘Surfaces’ wizard:

substeps.instruction: Leave first screen at default.
Select the nuclear stain channel.
Enable ‘Smooth’ and set ‘Surfaces Detail’ to 0.5 µm.
Measure nuclear diameter in Slice view and record the value.
Enable ‘Background Subtraction (Local Contrast)’ and set ‘Diameter of largest sphere which fits into the object’ to the measured diameter.
Adjust the background threshold until all nuclei are covered.
Enable ‘Split touching objects’; set ‘Seed Points Diameter’ to the same measured diameter.
Add a ‘Quality’ filter and drag until every nucleus has an object.
Finish the wizard and name the surfaces ‘nuclei’.

steps.title: Identify nuclear mRNAs (optional)
steps.instruction: Separate nuclear from cytoplasmic mRNA and translation‑site spots:

substeps.instruction: Select ‘SunTag mRNA spots’ and run the Imaris X‑tension ‘Split spots into surface objects’.
Select ‘scFv spots co‑located’ and run the same X‑tension.

steps.title: Export Imaris data
steps.instruction: Export spot and surface tables ensuring required columns are saved:

substeps.instruction: Export ‘SunTag mRNA spots’ (and, if used, ‘SunTag mRNA spots inside Surfaces’). Include files starting with ‘Position’ and all ‘Intensity*’ files.
Export ‘scFv spots co‑located’ (and, if used, ‘scFv spots co‑located inside Surfaces’). Include ‘Position’ and ‘Intensity*’ files.
Export the ‘nuclei’ surface data. Include ‘Position’ and all files beginning with ‘Ellipsoid Axis’.

steps.title: Remove nuclear mRNAs (optional)
steps.instruction: Run the remove_nuclear.py script to separate cytoplasmic and nuclear mRNA spots:

substeps.instruction: Create a folder containing the exported ‘SunTag mRNA spots’ (and the ‘inside Surfaces’ folder if present).
Open an Anaconda Prompt, type ‘python’, drag‑and‑drop remove_nuclear.py, then drag‑and‑drop the folder created above.
The script creates ‘Suntag mRNA cytoplasmic spots’ and ‘Suntag mRNA nuclear spots’. Use the cytoplasmic folder for downstream analysis.
Repeat the same procedure for ‘scFv spots co‑located’ (and its inside‑Surfaces folder).

steps.title: Assign spots to nearest nuclei
steps.instruction: Run spotME_EmbryoMid.py to map mRNA and translation‑site spots to the closest nucleus:

substeps.instruction: Create a folder containing the ‘SunTag mRNA spots’ (or the cytoplasmic version) and the ‘nuclei’ surface files.
In an Anaconda Prompt, type ‘python’, drag‑and‑drop spotME_EmbryoMid.py, then drag‑and‑drop the folder.
Collect the output file ‘all_data_with_distance.txt’ from the ‘time_data’ subfolder.
Repeat the procedure with the ‘scFv spots co‑located’ data to obtain translated‑mRNA assignments.

steps.title: Prepare high‑magnification images
steps.instruction: In Fiji, open each Leica image and save the channels separately as .tif files:

substeps.instruction: Save the SunTag smFISH channel as ‘suntag.tif’.
Save the mNeonGreen (scFv‑mNG) channel as ‘ng.tif’.

steps.title: Detect translation sites with Airlocalize
steps.instruction: Quantify translation‑site fluorescence using Airlocalize:

substeps.instruction: Launch Airlocalize, choose ‘3D single image’.
Select the ‘ng.tif’ file.
In ‘Quantification Parameters’, keep the default ‘PSF Width (pix)’ (will be set later). Choose an output folder and enable ‘output image of spots’.
Determine the PSF: for ~10 translation sites, click the centre of each spot, choose ‘local gaussian fit’, record the fit result, then click ‘done’.
Set a detection threshold so all translation sites appear as red overlays while single proteins are excluded; click ‘done’.
The output folder will contain ‘spots.tif’, ‘.loc3’, ‘.par3’, and ‘.det’ files. Move all of them into a subfolder named ‘translation_sites’.

steps.title: Detect single proteins with Airlocalize
steps.instruction: Quantify fluorescence of individual scFv‑mNG proteins:

substeps.instruction: Repeat steps 36a‑b (open Airlocalize, select ‘ng.tif’).

Either repeat the PSF determination (steps d‑e) or, to reuse the previously measured PSF, disable ‘set manually’ and paste the PSF values from the ‘.par3’ file generated in the translation‑site analysis.
Adjust the detection threshold so only single‑protein spots are identified; click ‘done’.
Move the resulting files into a subfolder called ‘single_proteins’.

steps.title: Detect mRNA spots with Airlocalize
steps.instruction: Identify SunTag smFISH mRNA foci for colocalization:

substeps.instruction: Repeat steps 36a‑b, this time selecting the ‘suntag.tif’ file.
Use the same parameter workflow (PSF determination, thresholding) as for translation sites.
Move the output files into a subfolder named ‘mRNA’.

steps.title: Calculate ribosome numbers
steps.instruction: Run the ribosome_number.py script to obtain ribosomes per translation site:

substeps.instruction: Open an Anaconda Prompt, type ‘python’, drag‑and‑drop ribosome_number.py, then drag‑and‑drop the folder containing the three subfolders ‘translation_sites’, ‘single_proteins’, and ‘mRNA’.

The script colocalizes translation‑site spots with mRNA spots, discards non‑colocalized translation sites, removes any translation‑site spots that appear in the single‑protein set, computes the median intensity of the remaining single proteins, and divides each translation‑site intensity by this median.
The result is saved as ‘num_ribo.csv’ containing the number of ribosomes per translation site.

steps.title: Apply ribosome correction factor
steps.instruction: Correct ribosome counts for partially translated SunTag repeats:

substeps.instruction: Compute correction factor = (lengthSunTagCDS × 0.5 + lengthhbCDS) / lengthtotal (assumes uniform ribosome distribution).
Divide each ribosome number in ‘num_ribo.csv’ by this factor to obtain the final ribosome count per site.

steps.title: Create nuclear surfaces for live imaging
steps.instruction: In Imaris, generate time‑resolved nuclear surfaces with tracking:

substeps.instruction: Start the ‘Surface’ wizard, enable ‘Track Surfaces (over Time)’.
Select the His‑RFP channel.
Enable ‘Smooth’ and set ‘Surfaces Detail’ to 1 µm.
Measure nuclear diameter in Slice view.
Enable ‘Background Subtraction’; set ‘Diameter of largest sphere which fits into the object’ to the measured diameter.
Adjust the threshold so nuclei are selected in all frames; verify across time points.
Enable ‘Split touching Objects (Region Growing)’ and set ‘Seed Points Diameter’ to the measured diameter.
Filter by ‘Quality’ and use ‘Number of Voxels Img=1’ to discard small non‑nuclear objects.
In the ‘Tracking’ screen, choose Algorithm = ‘Autoregressive Motion’, Max Distance = 5 µm, Max Gap Size = 3 (suitable for nc11‑nc14 where nuclei move ≤5 µm per frame).
Finish the wizard.

steps.title: Detect translation spots in live movies
steps.instruction: Identify scFv‑mNG translation sites in each time point (no tracking):

substeps.instruction: Open the Imaris ‘Spots’ wizard and deselect ‘Track Spots (over Time)’.
Select the scFv‑mNG channel.
Measure translation‑site size in Slice view and enter as ‘Estimated XY diameter’; enable ‘Model PSF‑elongation along Z‑axis’ and ‘Background Subtraction’.
Apply filters (e.g., ‘Quality’, ‘Intensity Max’, ‘Intensity Sum’) and verify spot selection across all frames.
Complete the wizard.

steps.title: Export live‑imaging statistics
steps.instruction: Save spot statistics for downstream analysis:

substeps.instruction: In the Imaris ‘Statistics’ tab, choose the desired statistics (e.g., scFv‑mNG intensity, spot positions per time point).
Export the table to file.

steps.title: Track single translation sites
steps.instruction: Track individual translation sites over time and export their trajectories:

substeps.instruction: Open the Imaris ‘Spots’ wizard, enable ‘Track spots over time’.
Select the scFv‑mNG channel and estimate the XY diameter so the full fluorescence of each site is enclosed.
Apply filters (‘Quality’, ‘Intensity Sum’, ‘Intensity Max’) to retain sites throughout the movie.
Set tracking parameters: Algorithm = ‘Autoregressive Motion’, Maximum Distance = 5 µm, Max Gap Size = 2.
Finish tracking.
In the ‘Statistics’ tab, choose ‘Export all Statistics to file’ (include intensity, distance, speed, etc.).

steps.title: Correct fluorescence background (optional)
steps.instruction: Subtract background from translation‑site intensities:

substeps.instruction: Manually place identical‑volume spot objects in several background regions, measure their intensities, compute the average background value, and subtract it from each translation‑site intensity.
For semi‑automated background removal, refer to Hoppe and Ashe (2021b).
